about: Here It Comes is a selfie of a sweaty, wild-eyed man screaming at the camera in the flat red Australian outback while a towering brown dust tornado churns behind him. He looks equal parts terrified and thrilled, the face of someone who has accepted that disaster is about to hit and wants a record of it. The meme uses that frozen moment for any inevitable, approaching catastrophe: Monday morning, the credit card bill, the boss's calendar invite, the plot twist you saw coming.
origin: The frame is from a 2014 viral video of a man filming himself as a tornado approached in the outback. It was later revealed to be a staged marketing stunt for the film Into the Storm, produced by an Australian video company.
usage:
The top box names the incoming disaster. The bottom box is the reaction, usually "here it comes" or a scream.

It lands best with dread you can see coming from far away: Sunday night before a deadline, the first day after vacation, an exam you didn't study for, a patch that nerfs your main, a meeting that could have been an email. Making the top line very specific and the bottom line short and loud mirrors the screaming face.
ideas: the email after i said 'per my last email'
the patch that nerfs my main
the final exam i didn't study for
the credit card bill after the holidays
my mom finding my report card
